idea-plugin.name: Mutable State Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a real mutation (`.add`/`.put`/`.remove`/`.clear`/an array-index write) of a value returned by a getter that hands back one of its OWN mutable fields (`List`/`Map`/`Set`/array) directly -- the real `EI_EXPOSE_REP` bug class (SpotBugs' own name for it), but PROVEN exploited here, not just a getter shaped in a risky way (CWE-374/375).

Built on real interprocedural alias tracking: the getter can live in a completely different class/file than the caller -- real PSI method resolution crosses that boundary naturally, no custom whole-project graph needed for this one-hop shape. SpotBugs' own heuristic only checks the getter's shape and never verifies a caller actually mutates the result -- this plugin requires BOTH.

Stated honestly: SpotBugs (bytecode, CI/build-step only, not an inline IDE inspection) is the real, confirmed prior art for the getter-shape half of this check. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found that also verifies real exploitation.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Mutating a directly-returned internal mutable field
